title: Chicken Paprikash with Nokedli
summary: Chicken thighs are braised in a deeply paprika-flavoured onion sauce, finished with soured cream, and served with soft, hand-pinched nokedli dumplings.
equipment: large heavy casserole with lid (26-28 cm)
spätzle maker or colander with large holes

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
soured cream, plus extra to serve
fine sea salt or table salt
ingredients.note: about ¼ tsp, for the nokedli batter

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, for the cooking water

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Season the chicken with salt, then heat the oil and butter in the casserole over medium-high heat. Lightly brown the chicken for 2 minutes per side, then lift it out onto a plate.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.text: With the heat lowered to medium, cook the onions for 10-12 minutes, until soft and pale golden. Slow, even cooking here builds the sweetness that underpins the whole sauce.

steps.title: Bloom the paprika off the heat
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat completely before stirring in the sweet and hot paprika for 30 seconds. This matters more than it sounds: paprika scorches and turns bitter within seconds over direct heat, so pulling the pan away protects its colour and flavour.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken
steps.text: Add the red pepper, tomato, garlic and water, return the pan to the heat, then add the chicken back in with its juices. Cover and simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, until the chicken is tender and reaches at least 74°C.

steps.title: Make the nokedli batter
steps.text: While the chicken simmers, whisk the flour, eggs, water and ¼ tsp of salt into a thick, sticky batter, then let it rest for 10 minutes so the flour fully hydrates.

steps.title: Cook the nokedli
steps.text: Bring a large pan of water to the boil with the tablespoon of salt. Press the batter through a spätzle maker or a large-holed colander directly into the boiling water, in 2 batches, and cook for 2-3 minutes until the dumplings float to the surface. Lift them out with a slotted spoon and toss with the butter.

steps.title: Finish with soured cream
steps.text: Whisk the soured cream with the flour, then whisk in a ladleful of the hot sauce to warm it through gradually. Stir this mixture back into the pan and heat gently for 2-3 minutes without letting it boil - the flour is what stops the cream from splitting as it heats.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the chicken and sauce over the nokedli, with an extra spoonful of soured cream on top.

tips: Take the pan off the heat before adding the paprika - cooking it directly over the flame for even a few extra seconds can turn it bitter.
Temper the soured cream with a ladle of hot sauce before stirring it into the pan, so it doesn't split when it hits the heat.
Keep the final simmer gentle once the cream goes in; a hard boil at that stage will curdle it.
Rest the nokedli batter for the full 10 minutes so it's easier to press through the colander or spätzle maker.
safety: Check the chicken reaches 74°C in the braise rather than guessing from time alone, since thigh pieces vary in thickness.
storage: Keep the chicken with its sauce in the fridge for up to 3 days; the dumplings are best made fresh but will keep separately for a day. Reheat gently on the hob without boiling hard, until piping hot and 74°C throughout, to avoid splitting the sauce. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
